key_insight: A proactive, integrated care model for patients with complex needs was difficult to test because far fewer patients met eligibility criteria than expected, but it still improved collaboration with social work and was adopted by many practices.
clinical_relevance: For health systems caring for patients with multiple unmet needs, the study suggests that local context, referral pathways, and recruitment design can strongly shape whether integrated care programs are feasible and scalable.
method: Mixed-method process evaluation using the RE-AIM framework.
Combined validated questionnaires, routine care data, and semi-structured interviews.
Quantitative results were analyzed descriptively; interviews used inductive thematic content analysis.
evidence_signal: Only 153 of 1403 screened patients were eligible and 30 enrolled, so the evidence mainly reflects implementation/process findings rather than robust effectiveness or cost-effectiveness data.
watch_item: Low acute care use reduced eligibility and enrollment, limiting conclusions and indicating that the target population definition may need revision for local settings.
paper_title: Lessons learned from a trial on integrated and proactive care for patients with complex needs (Hotspotters project): a process evaluation
